title: Option to enable or disable "Automatically enable audio for newly connected devices" behavior
line: Sound settings now have an option to stop newly connected audio devices from becoming the default, when the system's WirePlumber supports it.
explanation: On PipeWire, WirePlumber makes a newly connected device the default whenever its priority is higher than the current default's and no device the user chose is available, so a USB or Bluetooth headset takes over as soon as it is plugged in. This is WirePlumber's policy, it has no setting for it, and the KCM's only related option drives a PulseAudio module that is hidden on PipeWire. The fix is split: a WirePlumber patch (wireplumber-upstream.patch, against WirePlumber master) adds a stream.switch-to-new-default-targets setting that keeps the current default while it is available, below the user's own selections, and plasma-pa adds an "Automatically switch to newly connected devices" option to the KCM's Configure… menu that toggles that setting through wpctl, shown only when the running WirePlumber reports it.

commits.message:
kcm: add an option to not switch to newly connected devices

WirePlumber makes a newly connected device with a higher priority the
default. The new option toggles WirePlumber's setting to keep the current
one instead, and is only shown when the running WirePlumber has it.

BUG: 516683

media.caption: Sound settings on PipeWire: no Configure… menu, so no way to turn automatic switching off
With the patched WirePlumber: new Configure… menu with "Automatically switch to newly connected devices", here unchecked
Plugging in a USB headset while the built-in speakers play: the headset becomes the default
Same with the option unchecked: the speakers stay the default, the headset is just listed
Option still unchecked: after choosing the headset, unplugging it (back to the speakers) and plugging it in again, the chosen headset comes back

review.text: Splitting the policy toggle into an upstream WirePlumber setting and exposing it conditionally in plasma-pa is the right architectural direction, and the proposed WirePlumber hook is well designed. However, the plasma-pa MR cannot be merged before the upstream WirePlumber issue/patch is filed and the setting name is accepted upstream, since stream.switch-to-new-default-targets does not exist in any WirePlumber version yet. On the plasma-pa side, WirePlumberSetting also has a QProcess teardown/concurrency issue and spawns wpctl unconditionally even on non-WirePlumber setups.
changes: Submit the WirePlumber proposal/patch upstream and wait for upstream confirmation of the setting name and behavior (linking the upstream issue/MR) before merging the plasma-pa UI change.

Fix QProcess lifetime and ordering in WirePlumberSetting::setValue() and load(): parenting wpctl to this kills an in-flight 'wpctl settings --save' if the KCM closes immediately after toggling (losing the change and logging a Qt warning), and rapid toggles can spawn concurrent wpctl processes that finish out of order.

Gate WirePlumberSetting loading on PipeWire/WirePlumber being active (e.g. Server.hasWirePlumber) instead of spawning wpctl on PulseAudio setups, and decouple configureButton.enabled so moduleManager.settingsSupported without configModuleLoaded cannot disable the WirePlumber action.

reviews.text: The diagnosis is right: on PipeWire this behaviour is WirePlumber policy, and the existing KCM option only drives a PulseAudio module. But the plasma-pa change depends on a setting, stream.switch-to-new-default-targets, that exists only in an unfiled local WirePlumber patch. Until upstream accepts it under that exact name, the toggle is hidden everywhere and the MR adds dead code keyed on a speculative name. Maintainers would also question shelling out to wpctl from the KCM and parsing its human-readable output ('Value: ... (Saved: ...)'), which can change between WirePlumber versions.
changes: File the WirePlumber issue or MR first and get the setting (name and semantics) accepted upstream, then link it in the plasma-pa MR, and hold the plasma-pa MR until then.

Once upstream settles, read and write the setting in a sturdier way than parsing wpctl's text output (for example the settings metadata through libpipewire, or wpctl's machine-readable output if it has one), or at least make the parsing tolerant of format changes.
Update the commit message and line to say the option needs a WirePlumber version that has this setting.
